title: Nile Cruise Direction: Luxor to Aswan or Reverse?
excerpt: A Nile cruise from Luxor to Aswan sails upstream in 4 nights from €610; Aswan to Luxor sails downstream in 3 from €500, with a flight to Cairo. Same temples, different pace.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

A Nile cruise visits the same temples in either direction: Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings, Edfu, Kom Ombo and Philae. The difference is time. Luxor to Aswan sails upstream, against the current, and is sold as 4 nights. Aswan to Luxor sails downstream, with the current, and is sold as 3 nights. On Sawa the two are not like for like: the 3-night Nile Discovery from Aswan (from €500) also includes a flight from Luxor to Cairo and a Cairo dinner cruise, while the 4-night Nile Majesty from Luxor (from €610) gives you the extra day on the river. Take the 4-night cruise if you can spare the day, and the 3-night cruise if you cannot or are heading back to Cairo.

UNESCO documents the temples and necropolis of ancient Thebes, including Luxor and its West Bank.

You have decided on a Nile cruise, and then the booking sites ask: Luxor to Aswan, or Aswan to Luxor? The photos look identical and one direction costs an extra night. This post compares the two itineraries and ends with a clear recommendation. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is a shared-departure marketplace for Egyptian day tours and packages, and it lists both directions.

Nile cruise Luxor to Aswan or Aswan to Luxor: the short answer

Let your calendar choose. Luxor to Aswan, upstream, takes 4 nights; Aswan to Luxor, downstream, takes 3. The extra night buys pace rather than extra sites: the upstream cruise splits Luxor over two easy days, while the downstream cruise packs the same route into four fuller days. With five days, cruise from Luxor; without them, cruising from Aswan drops none of the main temples.

Why the upstream cruise takes 4 nights and the downstream cruise takes 3

The Nile flows north, so a boat leaving Luxor for Aswan is sailing upstream against the current, and operators sell the roughly 200 km run as 4 nights. The same kind of boat leaving Aswan for Luxor runs with the current and is sold as 3 nights. (Guides quote the river distance as anything from 200 to 220 km.) Most of the sailing happens while you eat and sleep, so what you notice is the rhythm: the upstream cruise spreads Luxor over two days with long afternoon sails, while the downstream cruise puts Aswan into your arrival day and saves the grandest temples for last.

Luxor to Aswan: what the 4-night upstream route covers

Cruises from Luxor open with the biggest sites, then wind south through the Ptolemaic temples to a relaxed Aswan finish. Day by day, on the Nile Majesty 5-day cruise from Luxor:

  1. Day 1: East Bank, Luxor. Board on arrival, then Karnak, the largest religious complex of ancient Egypt, and Luxor Temple in the evening.
  2. Day 2: West Bank, Luxor. The Valley of the Kings, Queen Hatshepsut's temple at Deir el-Bahari and the Colossi of Memnon; afternoon sailing south. The standard Valley of the Kings ticket (EGP 750, about €12.50 at EGP 60 to the euro on 8 November 2026) covers three tombs; special tombs are not included, and Tutankhamun's is a separate ticket (EGP 700, about €11.70).
  3. Day 3: Edfu and Kom Ombo. Morning at the Temple of Horus at Edfu, reached by the carriage ride included on Nile Majesty, among the best-preserved temples in Egypt; afternoon at Kom Ombo, the double temple of Sobek the crocodile god and Horus the Elder.
  4. Day 4: Aswan. Philae, the Temple of Isis on Agilkia Island (moved block by block between 1977 and 1980 under UNESCO's rescue campaign), the High Dam and the Unfinished Obelisk.
  5. Day 5: Aswan. Breakfast and leave the boat. International flights are not included.

Who the 4-night cruise suits

Travellers with five days who want a calmer pace: both Luxor banks on separate days, and a finish in Aswan, the natural springboard to Abu Simbel. From €610 per person, full board and site tickets, as listed in November 2026. Drinks, tips and the optional balloon are extra.

Aswan to Luxor: what the 3-night downstream route covers

The downstream cruise builds to a crescendo, from riverside shrines to Karnak on your final full day. Day by day, on the Nile Discovery 4-day cruise from Aswan:

  1. Day 1: Aswan. Board, then the High Dam, the Unfinished Obelisk and Philae Temple in one day.
  2. Day 2: Kom Ombo and Edfu. Kom Ombo, which many boats visit late in the day, then the Temple of Horus at Edfu; overnight sailing north.
  3. Day 3: Karnak and Luxor Temple, the route's two grandest sites, linked by the restored Avenue of Sphinxes (reopened in 2021).
  4. Day 4: West Bank, Luxor, then Cairo. Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's temple and the Colossi of Memnon, then the included flight from Luxor to Cairo and a Cairo dinner cruise.

Who the 3-night cruise suits

Travellers with four days who need to get back to Cairo, and anyone who likes a big finish. The honest trade-off is fuller days: all three Aswan sights land on arrival day. From €500 per person, as listed in November 2026, with full board, a licensed Egyptologist guide, site tickets, the Luxor to Cairo flight and the Cairo dinner cruise.

Recommendation: if you have the extra day, take the 4-night cruise from Luxor: same temples, gentler pace, Abu Simbel within easy reach at the finish. Take the 3-night cruise from Aswan when the calendar decides, or when you need to end in Cairo: at €500 with the flight back included, it is also the cheaper of the two.

How to choose: flights, Abu Simbel and sightseeing order

Flights and start or end city

Most travellers fly down from Cairo (about 1 hr 15 min to Luxor and about 1 hr 30 min to Aswan), and the direction decides where you finish. Nile Discovery ends with an included flight from Luxor to Cairo; Nile Majesty ends in Aswan, with your onward travel to arrange. Boat schedules matter as much as preference: Sawa's listings board in Luxor on Monday and Saturday and in Aswan on Wednesday and Friday (as listed in November 2026).

Fitting in Abu Simbel

Abu Simbel is included in neither cruise, and the cruises take no add-on extensions. The temples of Ramses II and Nefertari lie about 280 km south of Aswan, 3.5 to 4 hours by road each way, so they fit most easily after the 4-night cruise ends in Aswan, or before boarding the 3-night one. The Aswan to Abu Simbel day tour runs about 9 hours with hotel pickup in Aswan, from €50 per person, as listed in November 2026: Aswan to Abu Simbel: Temples of Ramses II and Nefertari. It is a separate departure, so book flights only after each date confirms.

Three river details most guidebooks miss:

  • Kom Ombo late in the day. Many boats call at Kom Ombo in the late afternoon or evening, when the temple on its bend of the Nile looks very different from daylight. The Ministry lists the neighbouring Crocodile Museum as open until 21:00.
  • The Esna lock and Edfu's carriages. Every Luxor to Aswan cruise passes the Esna lock, about 55 to 60 km south of Luxor. Most ships now pass in around two hours, depending on river traffic, so the day's timings can shift. At Edfu many passengers ride a horse-drawn carriage from the quay to the temple (Nile Majesty includes one); some visitors have welfare concerns about the horses, so ask your guide.
  • Boats differ on Luxor's order. On 3-night cruises some boats do the East Bank first and some the West Bank, so confirm before booking.

How to do either direction with Sawa Tours

Both cruises run on Sawa as shared departures: your group of up to 8 sails on a shared five-star ship and does the excursions together with its guide. Sawa keeps a fixed catalogue, owns the calendar and sets the prices, which are fixed per traveller. Reserving a seat is free, with no card, and nothing is charged before the GoAhead, the moment four travellers (people, not bookings) have reserved a date. As packages, the cruises take a 25% deposit at the GoAhead, and the balance is due 14 days before departure. A date must reach four travellers by 30 days before; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and another date is suggested. Groups never exceed eight, and when a departure fills, a new independent departure opens. Solo cabins are confirmed in the booking, with no promise in advance.

Cancel 30 or more days before departure and there is no charge; from 29 to 15 days you lose half the deposit (12.5%); at 14 days or fewer, or if you do not show, the deposit (25%) is retained. Some components, such as flights and cabins, may become non-refundable earlier; this is disclosed before payment. Payment is by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. Several agencies can sell seats on a departure, and it is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. Sawa works with a founding operating partner, Capital Travel Service (licence 2179). See the terms and the GoAhead promise. The full rules are in the GoAhead explained. The verdict on Nile cruise direction

Both directions deliver the same ten sites, so the choice is about days, not temples. Luxor to Aswan takes 4 nights, sails upstream and ends in Aswan, the base for Abu Simbel. Aswan to Luxor takes 3 nights, sails downstream and saves Karnak for last. Next step: browse forming Nile cruise departures on Sawa or start your own date on the Nile Majesty cruise from Luxor. faq.q: Do both directions really visit the same temples?
faq.a: Yes. Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's temple, the Colossi of Memnon, Edfu, Kom Ombo, Philae, the High Dam and the Unfinished Obelisk appear on both the 4-night and the 3-night itineraries. Only the order, the pace and the number of nights change, plus, on Sawa, what is bundled around the cruise: Nile Discovery adds the flight to Cairo and a dinner cruise.

faq.q: Is a 3-night Nile cruise long enough?
faq.a: For the headline temples, yes: you lose none of them. The trade-off is pace, because all three Aswan sights happen on arrival day. If you want slower Luxor time, or Abu Simbel without rushing, add a night in Aswan or take the 4-night cruise.

faq.q: Can I start a Nile cruise on any day of the week?
faq.a: No. Nile cruises sail on fixed weekly schedules. As listed in November 2026, Sawa's cruises board in Luxor on Mondays and Saturdays and in Aswan on Wednesdays and Fridays. Plan your domestic flights around those boarding days.

faq.q: Can I join a Nile cruise solo?
faq.a: Yes. The price is fixed per traveller, and a solo cabin is confirmed in the booking, so check it for your date before you pay; Sawa makes no promise in advance. A shared departure of up to eight travellers gives a solo traveller a ready-made group for the excursions and the guide.

faq.q: What happens if the cruise departure doesn't fill?
faq.a: Nothing is charged until a date reaches four travellers and gets the GoAhead. A cruise date must reach four by 30 days before departure; if it does not, it is cancelled, you pay nothing and Sawa suggests another date. Once a date has confirmed, it is not cancelled for low numbers. Read why Egypt group tours get cancelled for the background.
